newsitem.title: LEBANON: Iraqi athletes to leave Lebanon border back home.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi athletes to leave Lebanon border back home.

text.p: Iraqi athletes stranded at a Lebanese frontier post after Lebanon denied them entry to compete in the Pan Arab Games are expected to leave back to Iraq on Saturday evening.
No announcement has been made but journalists overheard delegation leader Assil Tabra as telling trainers the group should leave after the official opening of the games in Beirut at 0530 gmt.
Tabra told them he was in contact with Syrian officials who would accomodate the team temporarily before making their final trip back to Baghdad.

"Up until this moment, we have had no official response neither from the Lebanese government nor from the Arab League. We are still waiting to know if we are excluded from the games," Tabra told reporters.
"We are not begging for participation but we believe it is a right granted to us by the Arab League charter," Tabra added.
The two-weeks-long Pan Arab Games, which are held every four years, are the first major international event staged in the Lebanese capital since the end of the 1975-90 civil war.
The 97 athletes looked tired after a night in the cold dusty Masnaa post.
"We slept on the ground, with no blankets. It was cold. It was not a good ending for our long and tiring trip from Iraq," player Khaled Zahra, 25, told Reuters.
The Iraqi athletes arrived at Masnaa at 8.30 a.m. (0530 GMT) on Friday in three buses after crossing Syria in a 20-hour drive from Baghdad.
Some of them kept busy at this deserted area by exercising. Others lounged around in circles and chanted Iraqi popular rhymes.
A Lebanese foreign ministry official said on Wednesday Beirut has been under pressure from Saudi Arabia and Kuwait to exclude the Iraqis from the games.

Both Kuwait and Saudi Arabia, Gulf War foes of Iraq and among the most generous Arab financiers of Lebanon's postwar reconstruction, threatened to boycott the games if Iraq competed, the official said.
"Kuwaitis are scared...Iraqis hold steadfast," the athletes sang at the borders.
Embarrassed Lebanese officials in Beirut avoided reporters seeking clarification whether the Iraqis would be allowed in.
If Iraq competes there will be 20 countries participating.

Tabra showed reporters on Friday invitations to the games and several confirmations which he said Iraq had received since February from the Arab League, Lebanon's education ministry and the Games organising committee.
